title: No visual distinction between the "preferred device zero volume" state and the "global mute" state
line: Pressing the Mute key after lowering the volume to 0% now unmutes the speakers at a low volume instead of showing "Audio Muted" again.
explanation: Lowering the volume to 0% mutes the preferred device itself. The Mute key only toggles global mute, which doesn't touch a device it didn't mute, so both presses left the device at 0% and muted and showed the same "Audio Muted" OSD. Now, when global mute is off and the preferred device is at 0%, the Mute key raises its volume by one step and unmutes it, as the reporter's second option suggested.

commits.message:
kded: Unmute a device at 0% by raising its volume with the Mute key

Lowering the volume to 0 mutes the device, and pressing Mute then only
toggled global mute, which left it muted with the same OSD. If the device
is at 0%, the Mute key now raises its volume by one step and unmutes it.

BUG: 506791

media.caption: Volume down to 0%, then Mute twice: "Audio Muted" all three times
Same steps: the first Mute unmutes at 5%, the second mutes again

review.text: Merging the states by raising a 0% device on Mute is a reasonable reading of the reporter's second option, and it uses the existing helpers. However, the new branch checks only volume == 0, not whether the device is muted. A sink left at 0% but unmuted (for example from pavucontrol) would now become audible at one step when the user presses Mute, which is the opposite of what the key promises.
changes: Only take the raise-and-unmute path when the preferred sink is both at 0% and muted (sink->isMuted()); otherwise keep enabling global mute.
